messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert triggered: PD-99431 - metric: redis.accept_queue.aggregate > 1000 (3m) AND pgbouncer.conn_wait spike across frontend pool. Auto-alerting aggregate rule fired.

olivia: Ack — I'm oncall, jumping in. @sam @maria can you confirm customer impact?

sam: Looking at metrics now. rps spiked ~3x starting 15:25 UTC. redis accept-queue peaked ~1100 across primaries, connected_clients ~9.9k, maxclients set to 10k. p95 latency ~800ms on some shards.

maria: Confirmed from service side — about ~8-12% of read requests in us-west returning timeouts/circuit-breaker trips. Writes appear fine. Not yet full failover but user-facing read degradation for a subset of tenants.

ryan: PD shows repeat alerts — looks like flapping across hosts, causing multiple PD notifications (PD loop). We should silence the noisy rule while we mitigate to avoid paging the entire rotation.

olivia: Plan: 1) scale read-only redis replicas (ephemeral) 2) throttle suspected batch job fanout 3) bump pgbouncer client limits temporarily 4) enable read-only fallback for non-critical endpoints in us-west. I'll coordinate.

sam: Running quick checks/commands now:
```
# redis client summary
redis-cli -h cache-primary info clients | egrep 'connected_clients|maxclients|blocked_clients'
redis-cli -h cache-primary client list | wc -l
redis-cli -h cache-primary slowlog get 20
```

sam: Output: connected_clients:9982, maxclients:10000, blocked_clients:132. slowlog shows many long-running commands (SORT/KEYS/large ZRANGE). Looks like a bad batch job/maintenance window triggered a large key scan.

maria: I see a scheduled batch that kicked at 15:24 (job-runner v2.1.4) — it fanouts lots of small lookups into redis. Pausing the job now. @ryan can you pin the job to a rolling release/rollback?

ryan: Throttling the job via feature-flag: rolling the flag to 10% and pausing immediate runs. Also creating a temporary rate-limit for the job producers.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: PD-99431 acknowledged by olivia. Next escalation in 30m if still unacked.

olivia: Triggering scaleup: infra-svc/redis-readers autoscale +3 nodes (ephemeral). Also increasing kernel backlog knobs as precaution.

infra-bot: Autoscale accepted: requested 3 instances in asg redis-readers; estimated ready in ~90s.

sam: Post-scale update (after 60s): accept_queue aggregate dropped from ~1100 -> ~130. p95 latency improved to ~120ms. Applying temporary pgbouncer bump to reduce conn_wait backlog.
```
# pgbouncer config patch (example)
kubectl -n infra exec pgbouncer-frontend-0 -- psql -c "SHOW POOLS;"
kubectl -n infra patch cm pgbouncer-config --patch '{"data":{"max_client_conn":"5000"}}'
```

maria: Enabling read-only fallback for non-critical queries in us-west (feature toggle). This will route heavy reads to read-replicas and serve stale-but-safe results for a short window. Notifying support and docs.

olivia: Customer impact summary: intermittent read timeouts for ~8% of requests in us-west for ~22 minutes starting at 15:25 UTC. No writes lost, no billing/SSO impact. Error budget hit for a small set of tenants; majority back to baseline after scale + job throttle.

sam: Action items logged: INFRA-1879 (suppress aggressive PD loop by adding suppress window on cluster-aggregate acceptqueue), INFRA-1880 (auto-pause abusive batch jobs if acceptqueue > 500 for >2m), RUNBOOK-22 (pgbouncer emergency bump steps).

ryan: Also recommend edit to alert rule: require sustained >500 for 3m AND at least 60% of shards affected to reduce noisy pages. I'll open the alert PR.

maria: Postmortem draft will include timeline, root cause (unthrottled batch job + low alert dedupe threshold), mitigations, and follow-ups. Dashboards and links: https://grafana.internal/d/redis-cluster/overview, https://pd.internal/pd/99431

olivia: Thanks all. I'll keep PD open until we confirm stable for 30m then close and handoff to infra for postmortem. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: PagerDuty: PD-99431 closed by olivia. Duration 39m. Handoff: infra team (owner: sam) for follow-up.

sam: Ack — will own postmortem and follow-ups. Noted next steps and will schedule a short remediation sync.
